recipes.name: Pollock pancakes (Dongtaejeon)
ingredients: Kosher salt, a few pinches for the fish and a few pinches for the eggs
1 to 2 tablespoons canola oil (or vegetable oil), plus more as needed
instructions: Take 1 frozen pollock fillet (about 200 grams' worth) out of the package, rinse it in cold water, and set aside for about 20 minutes, until slightly thawed but still firm and slightly icy. This makes it easier to slice thinly.

Slice it into pieces at a 45 degree angle. Slicing takes about 5 minutes. You should get 8-9 pieces that are ⅛ inch thick x 2 inches x 3 inches. Thin slices cook quickly, so the pan frying takes only about 5 minutes.
Sprinkle a few pinches of salt and a bit of ground black pepper over the slices.
Place ⅓ cup of flour in a bowl. Add the fish slices and mix by hand to coat them with flour.
Beat 2 eggs in a small bowl with a few pinches of salt.
Heat up a non-stick pan over medium high heat.
Add 1-2 tbs canola oil to the pan. Dip each pollock slice in the beaten egg and place it onto the heated pan.
Lower the heat and cook for 1 minute. Turn it over with a spatula and cook 1 more minute. Add more oil if needed, and put more egg mixture on top of each slice if you want to make it yellower.
Serve hot, warm, or cool. To make a fast dipping sauce, mix 1 tablespoon soy sauce and ½ tablespoon vinegar in a bowl.

ingredient_sections.text: Preparation time: about 25 minutes, including 20 minutes for partial thawing and 5 minutes for slicing Cooking time: about 5 minutes Total time: about 30 minutes
Kosher salt, a few pinches for the fish and a few pinches for the eggs
1 to 2 tablespoons canola oil (or vegetable oil), plus more as needed

Heat up a non-stick pan over medium high heat.
Add 1-2 tbs canola oil to the pan. Dip each pollock slice in the beaten egg and place it onto the heated pan.

Lower the heat and cook for 1 minute. Turn it over with a spatula and cook 1 more minute. Add more oil if needed, and put more egg mixture on top of each slice if you want to make it yellower. *tip: the leftover egg mixture and flour will be good batter for another pancake. Chop up any of your favorite vegetables and mix it with the batter and make a pancake! If you use chopped kimchi, it is kimchi pancake (kimchijeon)! Cooking is too easy, huh? : )
To make a fast dipping sauce, mix 1 tbs of soy sauce and ½ tbs vinegar in a bowl.
Refrigerate leftovers promptly in an airtight container and use within 3 to 4 days. You can also freeze them for about 1 month.

To reheat refrigerated dongtaejeon, add a little oil to a skillet and cook for about 2 minutes, turning the pieces until golden and hot all the way through. For frozen dongtaejeon, thaw in the refrigerator first, then reheat in the skillet the same way. Cook a little longer if needed to heat the center thoroughly.
If you are in a hurry, you can use the microwave, but the pancakes will lose some of their crispness.
